Apple today announced the M6 chip, the first in a new generation of chipsets that will eventually include the A20 Pro for the iPhone 18 Pro. This article looks at what performance gains we can expect from the iPhone 18 Pro, via the M6.

M6 hints at major performance and efficiency gains for the iPhone 18 Pro with A20 Pro

Although it's still months until September, Apple today surprised us with two new product launches: a brand new Mac mini and a Mac Studio. (Now available for pre-order: Mac mini, Mac Studio.)

The Mac mini is powered by Apple's new-generation M6 chip, the same chipset family that will eventually power the iPhone 18 Pro's A20 Pro.

Below is what Apple's press release says:

The M6 uses the most advanced 2-nanometer process technology, packing higher transistor density onto a smaller die for major leaps in performance and energy efficiency. The M6 also introduces the first dual 16-core Neural Engines, delivering up to 2x peak compute over the previous generation for faster on-device AI workflows. ⋯⋯ The M6 features a new 12-core CPU architecture, two more cores than the M5, comprising 2 super cores, 4 performance cores and 6 efficiency cores, delivering the world's fastest single-threaded performance and up to 1.2x faster multi-threaded performance than the M5.

Ultimately, the M6 will demonstrate that it outperforms the new A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro. This is generally the case with M-series chips for Mac and iPad.

However, since the M6 and A20 Pro are in the same chipset family, the upgrades announced for the M6 should also be reflected in the A20 Pro.

Most notably, the A20 Pro will use the same new 2-nanometer process highlighted by the M6, delivering "major leaps in performance and energy efficiency."

We've been assuming that moving to 2-nanometer would yield bigger improvements than in previous years, and the M6 details confirm exactly that.

The A20 Pro may not have the exact same CPU and GPU core counts as the M6, and the dual 16-core Neural Engines are also unknown. But with 2-nanometer process technology, it should deliver significant improvements in the two areas Apple highlighted today: performance and efficiency.

How big the year-over-year gains will be in practice is hard to say. But when the iPhone 18 Pro is unveiled in a few weeks, expect performance and efficiency to be the key upgrades for the A20 Pro.
